title: VPC Segmentation, BGP Topology, and Cross-Region Failover Playbook
author: Priya Narang
body:
Overview
========
This document is a deployment and operations playbook for VPC network segmentation, BGP-based routing topologies, and controlled cross-region failover for Redwood private deployments (VPC and hybrid on-prem/VPC setups). It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and network architects who are installing or operating Redwood Private control planes and inference clusters with multi-region resilience requirements.

Goals and scope
----------------
- Provide a prescriptive, testable design for VPC segmentation and BGP peering suitable for Redwood Private control planes and GPU serving clusters.
- Define a deterministic, low-risk cross-region failover procedure (planned and unplanned) including DNS and routing cutover.
- Document observability checks, SLO impacts, rollback steps, and post-failover validation.
- Applicable to customer deployments using: AWS VPC with Transit Gateway, Azure vWAN/ExpressRoute, GCP VPC with Cloud Router, and on-prem transit fabrics that speak BGP.

Assumptions and preconditions
-----------------------------
- Customer provides at least two isolated regions (AZs or on-prem sites) with routable connectivity (IPsec/DirectConnect/Interconnect or private fiber).
- Each site has a documented ASN and BGP peering capability.
- Control plane nodes (api/console/telemetry) and runtime GPU pools are on separate segments/subnets.
- IP addressing plan and CIDR allocations have been reviewed with Redwood network engineer (see Related Pages).

Key services and SLOs impacted by failover
-----------------------------------------
- Redwood Control Plane API (redwood-api): 99.95% regional SLO; cross-region failover will incur 10–60s DNS propagation window.
- Inference Runtime Gateway (runtime-gw): 99.9% availability; active-routing cutover may cause transient requests to stall for up to 5s per active connection.
- Telemetry ingestion (telemetry-ingest): best-effort during failover; retention of telemetry is required for rollback analysis.

High-level design recommendations
--------------------------------
1) Segmentation model
   - Control plane (management): dedicated private subnets, not NATed to customer internet.
   - Runtime/Serving: GPU worker subnets with strict egress rules (only to control plane, upstream model repos, and container registries).
   - Observability: telemetry and metrics collector subnets with access to internal KMS and SIEM.
   - Admin/ops: bastion and jump-host subnets with MFA-protected SSH and limited CIDR access.

2) BGP topology and AS planning
   - Use distinct ASNs per site (customer ASN or private ASN range).
   - Establish two BGP sessions per region: one to the regional transit gateway and one to the customer edge/router for redundancy (active/active preferred).
   - Advertise /22 (or appropriate aggregated route) for the serving subnets to reduce RIB churn.

3) ECMP and route preference
   - Prefer local region path by setting local-pref 200 on local-edge; set remote region local-pref 100.
   - Use MED to influence path selection for inter-region traffic where necessary.

4) Graceful prefix withdrawal
   - Before a failover, withdraw BGP routes in a staged manner to avoid microloops: withdraw serving prefixes, wait 30s, then withdraw control-plane prefixes if full failover is needed.

Configuration examples
----------------------
Note: below examples are illustrative. Replace placeholders with customer ASNs, IPs, and interface names.

JunOS example (announce serving CIDR):
```
set routing-options autonomous-system 65010
set protocols bgp group TGW-PEER type external
set protocols bgp group TGW-PEER peer-as 65100
set protocols bgp group TGW-PEER neighbor 10.0.0.2
set policy-options policy-statement EXPORT-SERVING term 1 from route-filter 10.20.0.0/22 exact
set policy-options policy-statement EXPORT-SERVING term 1 then accept
set policy-options policy-statement EXPORT-SERVING term 2 then reject
set protocols bgp group TGW-PEER export EXPORT-SERVING
```

Cisco IOS XR (set local-pref for site):
```
router bgp 65010
 bgp router-id 10.0.0.1
 neighbor 192.0.2.2 remote-as 65100
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.20.0.0/22
  neighbor 192.0.2.2 route-policy SET-LOCALPREF out
!
route-policy SET-LOCALPREF
 set local-preference 200
end-policy
```

DNS and service discovery guidance
----------------------------------
- Use DNS failover with low TTL (30s) for control-plane endpoints. For runtime endpoints serving unpinned customer traffic, prefer Anycast or global load balancer fronting region-local IPs.
- Recommended DNS pattern: api.<customer>.redwood.internal -> CNAME to region-specific endpoint (api-us-east1.<customer>.redwood.internal).
- TTLs: control-plane endpoints 30–60s; long-lived streaming sessions should be routed via a sticky reverse-proxy to avoid mid-stream DNS rebinds.

Planned failover procedure (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------
1) Preflight (T-60 to T-15 minutes)
   - Notify stakeholders (Support, Customer Eng, Security) and create incident channel.
   - Confirm recent config backups exist for routers, firewalls, and Redwood control plane.
   - Verify health of target region (CPU/GPU capacity, control-plane quorum, disk free > 20%).
   - Run a BGP neighbor status check: ensure all peers show Established for > 5 minutes.

2) Stage 1 — Traffic steering to target region (T-10 minutes)
   - On primary region edge, lower local-pref for serving prefixes to 50 (soft preference).
   - On target region, set local-pref to 200 for serving prefixes.
   - Wait 60s and monitor BGP table for the expected path change.
   - Validate that a small fraction (5–10%) of test traffic reaches target region by using synthetic probes.

3) Stage 2 — Full cutover (T=0)
   - Withdraw serving prefixes from primary region if required (withdraw step takes effect in seconds across backbone).
   - Update DNS CNAMEs to point control-plane records to target region.
   - Scale up ephemeral routing proxies in target region if needed (runtime-gw replicas +20%).

4) Post-cutover validation (T+0 to T+30 minutes)
   - Validate control-plane API health endpoints: /healthz and /metrics return 200 and expected scrape values.
   - Run end-to-end inference smoke tests (10 warm requests across multiple models).
   - Confirm telemetry ingestion within 5 minutes of cutover.
   - Observe latency p95 and error-rate for 30 minutes; compare to baseline.

Unplanned failover (SRE runbook)
--------------------------------
Trigger: partial or full region outage detected (cloud provider alert, BGP flap, or circuit failure). Follow these steps: 
1) Triage and confirm outage via provider console and BGP session state.
2) Promote target region by setting target local-pref=250 and withdraw on impacted region.
3) If DNS has long TTLs, perform emergency DNS override using global load balancer's traffic steering or short-lived synthetic CNAME updates.
4) If control-plane quorum is at risk, promote a read-only control-plane mode to preserve API read paths and prevent split-brain (see Quorum Guidance below).

Rollback and recovery
---------------------
- To rollback after an accidental failover: reverse local-pref adjustments, re-announce original prefixes, and restore DNS records to previous CNAMEs.
- Validate node-by-node state: ensure control-plane leader election stable and KV-store has matching revision number across nodes.
- If the customer network appliance has stale BGP sessions, clear the BGP session (clear bgp neighbor) during a maintenance window to avoid route leaks.

Quorum guidance (control-plane state)
-------------------------------------
- Redwood control plane uses consensus (raft/etcd-style) with odd-numbered node sets. During cross-region failover, ensure at least a majority of voting nodes are reachable in the promoted region to avoid split-brain.
- If majority is not possible, switch to read-only API mode: set environment variable REDWOOD_API_READ_ONLY=true on the control-plane service until quorum restored.

Testing and validation matrix
-----------------------------
| Test | Trigger | Expected result | Run frequency | Owner |
|------|---------|-----------------|---------------|-------|
| BGP session flapping simulation | Remove peer on secondary | Route converges to primary in <90s | quarterly | SRE |
| Partial prefix withdrawal | Withdraw subset of serving CIDR | 5–10% traffic shifts to target | monthly | Customer Eng |
| Full failover DR test | Planned region shutdown | End-to-end pass within 10m | yearly | SRE + Customer |

Observability and runbook checks
--------------------------------
- Dashboards to monitor during events: BGP peer count, RIB size, route origin changes, API 5xx rate, runtime queue depth, active KV-store term, and control-plane leader id.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - BGP peers Established < expected -> P1 pager
  - Control-plane leader changes > 3 in 5m -> P1 pager
  - API 5xx > 1% for 10m -> P1 (investigate routing)

Operational notes and gotchas
----------------------------
- Avoid frequent route churn: do not flip local-pref more than once per 5 minutes unless scripted and tested.
- Watch for asymmetric routing when only control-plane prefixes are redirected — clients may reach runtime data-plane over a different fabric causing MTU or path-MTU issues.
- IPsec and hardware acceleration on customer edges can mask packet drops; validate by testing end-to-end TCP sessions rather than only ICMP.

Appendix: Example cutover checklist (short)
------------------------------------------
- [ ] Create incident channel and notify stakeholders
- [ ] Snapshot control-plane data directories
- [ ] Confirm BGP sessions Established on target region
- [ ] Set target local-pref=200 on target edge
- [ ] Lower primary local-pref to 50 and monitor for 60s
- [ ] Update DNS (if required) and verify CNAME resolution
- [ ] Run 10 inference smoke requests and validate results
- [ ] Monitor telemetry for 30m and keep channel open for 2h
